title: Can I MASTER Chess960?
summary: Player plays five online Chess960 (Fischer Random) games vs ~1600-1700 humans at bullet speed, tracked by a 1-5 game counter after a '960 Positions' title card.
rules: Back rank pieces shuffled randomly, same shuffle mirrored for both sides; pawns normal.
Bishops on opposite colours; king somewhere between the two rooks.
Castling: king and rook end on the standard castled squares (g1/f1 or c1/d1) regardless of start squares; all squares between must be empty and king not in/through check.

opponent.name: online human opponents (chess.com Variants)
opponent.avatar_description: generic chess.com user avatar; random human usernames

setup: Random Chess960 position; example from frames: back rank Q B R K B N R N (QBRKBNRN) mirrored for black, pawns on ranks 2/7.
evidence: Frames (research/frames/visual_*.jsonl): {"start_pieces": "shuffled back rank (example shown: Q B R K B N R N), pawns normal", "special": ["'960 Positions' title card", "1-5 game counter", "very short clocks (0:05.9, 0:21) \u2014 bullet"], "opponent_ui": "humans nurludo (1721), DaryabiTB (1628); me 1571-1604", "notes": "Thumbnail '960' stopwatch."}. No rules.jsonl line.  Rules are the standard published rules of this variant (frames show the chess.com variant; transcript unavailable), so rule details are from the variant's known definition.
